title: A client and server
hints: Keep one map from client id to its state (name if joined, recent line times). Work through each line in the order of the specification: limits first, then the command, then the per-command checks. A small `reply` lambda and a `toOthers` helper keep the many branches short.

Do the rate limit by dropping times that are 1000 ms or more in the past from the front of the client's deque, checking whether 5 remain, and then recording the current line's time whatever the outcome.
requirements: The handshake checks the version and the name, and refuses duplicates ignoring case.
Every command is validated, with the exact error replies above.
Rate limiting and line length limits protect the server from a flooding client.
Joins, messages and departures reach the right clients, in a defined order.
Clients that quit or vanish are cleaned up and announced.
stretch: Make it real: a named pipe server (an accept loop and a thread per client, or overlapped I/O) with line framing, a small console client, and the security of lesson 5.05: a pipe descriptor limited to the current user and `FILE_FLAG_FIRST_PIPE_INSTANCE`. Then test it with the fault-injection ideas of lesson 6.04.
